scenario.prompt_to_agent:
router11 (one of the OSPF spokes) shows no routing path to
external networks. Operators report router11 has OSPF Full
adjacencies but cannot ping the Campus 2 server-side SVI
(10.5.0.254). Other spokes (router10, router8) reach it fine.
Find the difference on router11.

injection.command: ip route del default 2>/dev/null; vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "no default-information originate" -c "exit" -c "exit" 2>/dev/null

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router11 default route
Mechanism: router11 originally had a default route (either
  static or learned via OSPF default-information). When
  removed, any destination not explicitly in router11's RIB
  has no next hop. OSPF adjacencies stay up because they
  use directly-connected links, but transit to 10.5.0.254
  (which is reachable only via the default + intermediate
  hops) fails.
Localization: router11
Root cause: default route removed on router11
Fix: `ip route add default via <next-hop>` or re-enable
  default-information learning
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip route add default via <next-hop>` or re-enable
  default-information learning

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — that router11 has OSPF Full adjacencies but cannot ping the
Campus 2 server-side SVI at 10.5.0.254 while router10 and router8 reach it fine —
does not correspond to any real fault in the lab.

Direct evidence contradicts every element of the complaint. Router11 holds two stable
Full/DR OSPF adjacencies (with hub router17 on 10.1.0.0/24 and with WAN router1 on
10.1.1.0/24), both up for over 14 minutes with empty retransmit, request, and DB-summary
queues. Its routing table contains a correctly computed OSPF route to 10.5.0.0/24 at
metric [110/20] via 10.1.0.2 (router17), exactly the same path and cost as router10
([110/20] via 192.168.144.2) and router8 ([110/20] via 172.29.10.2). A live ping from
router11 to 10.5.0.254 succeeds with 0% packet loss, and traceroute confirms a clean
two-hop path: router11 → router17 → 10.5.0.254.

The OSPF link-state databases on all three spokes are cryptographically identical
(RouterLSA checksum 0x000501ad, NetworkLSA checksum 0x0005008b), meaning all routers
share exactly the same topology view. OSPF interface parameters (cost=10, Hello=10s,
Dead=40s, area 0, BROADCAST type, both interfaces active and non-passive) are uniform
across router11, router10, and router8. No iptables rules, distribute-lists, static
routes, or route filters exist on router11, and IP forwarding is enabled.

Root cause: There is no fault. The trouble ticket is based on a false premise — router11
is reachable to Campus 2 and behaves identically to the other spoke routers.

Corrective action: No configuration change required. The operator should re-verify
their test procedure; the network is operating correctly.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies and discusses router11 as the device under test and bases the diagnosis on its state.
The agent did not identify the default route on router11 as the affected component and instead asserted there was no fault.
Agent explicitly rules out an OSPF neighbor failure by showing Full adjacencies, matching LSDB checksums, healthy OSPF timers/queues, and successful ping/traceroute to the target.
Agent recommends no change, but the expected remediation is to add a default route or re-enable default-information learning, so the proposed fix does not match.

The agent's conclusion that router11 is functioning (reachability to 10.5.0.254) is well supported by observed pings, traceroute, OSPF neighbor/output, ip_forward and iptables outputs in the log.
